miniProject.title: Data-parallel training with overlapped buckets
miniProject.brief: Build data-parallel training in `parallel/` on the `comm/` layer: disjoint sharding, explicit averaging, bucketed overlap and honest timelines. This is the first distributed optimizer step in trainlab, and its oracle discipline carries into sharded and model-parallel sections.
steps: Shard the corpus with `DistributedSampler`, proving disjointness and union on every rank under both padding policies; call `set_epoch` each epoch and show epoch resume reproduces the interrupted order.

Fix a single-process oracle for a small model, then match it step for step with hand-rolled broadcast, shard, all-reduce average and a per-rank update; pass the CS336 DDP tests for plain and tied-weight models.

Hold the global batch fixed while accumulating over micro-steps with `no_sync` on non-final steps; prove equivalence with the oracle, show the mis-scoped variant still syncs, and check the loss-scaling rule.

Group gradients into buckets that all-reduce asynchronously during backward and match the oracle; compare launch counts across bucket caps, and bound a compressed hook plus a small PowerSGD experiment against vanilla averaging with accuracy evidence.

Record per-rank gradient-ready and bucket-collective intervals under fixed global work and label hidden against exposed communication; derive scaling efficiency from fixed-work runs and localize an injected slow rank, keeping GPU timing claims to runs with two or more GPUs.

Reduce rank shard losses and counts to one global metric with the correct denominator; reduce BatchNorm sums and counts by hand on CPU, where `SyncBatchNorm` rejects training input, and on your GPU convert with `convert_sync_batchnorm` before wrapping, and attribute a rank crash to its first cause from rank-tagged logs with bounded teardown.
deliverables: Disjoint sharding with sampler tests and the single-process oracle.
Explicit, bucketed and overlapped data-parallel steps with equivalence and timeline evidence.
Compression bounds, scaling-efficiency numbers and the crash-attribution log.

checks.name: CS336 Assignment 2 DDP tests
checks.note: Pass both model variants on CPU with the oracle comparison after every step.

checks.name: TensorTonic: Synchronize Data-Parallel Gradients
checks.note: Pass the public averaging cases before wiring the collective version.

checks.name: PyTorch DDP communication hooks PowerSGD experiment
checks.note: Run the register-and-compare example on CPU; keep error and accuracy evidence.

rubric.pass: Shards are proved disjoint with union coverage under both policies, and epoch resume reproduces the interrupted order.
rubric.strong: A seeded overlap is caught by the tests and padding tokens are excluded from the reported batch.

rubric.pass: Explicit, accumulated and bucketed steps each match the oracle within a stated tolerance, including tied weights.
rubric.strong: The suite passes repeatedly and the tolerance is derived from a rounding study, not guessed.

rubric.pass: Timelines label hidden against exposed intervals under fixed work, and launch counts follow the cap.
rubric.strong: A bucket-size crossover is measured with the losing side kept, and compression keeps its accuracy bound.

rubric.pass: Metrics use the global denominator, and the crash run names its first cause within a bounded time.
rubric.strong: A divergent-control hang is drilled and distinguished from a dead rank.

miniProject.feedsInto: Averaged data-parallel steps, the oracle habit and timelines feed sharded training, model parallelism and the capstone contribution baseline.
